requirement: EPIC-1 · Story 1.6 — Responsive two-pane layout + a11y baseline. Desktop shows the replica (left) and the 32-step grid (right) side by side; the layout collapses cleanly to a single stacked pane at narrow width so mobile is later config. Accessibility baseline: keyboard play (physical keys map to pads + a key toggles transport), a prefers-reduced-motion mode that swaps animated cues for a non-animated equivalent, AA contrast, target sizes that meet the minimum, and cues that carry shape + motion (not hue alone). The two-pane CSS grid + an 820px collapse already exist from story 1.1 — this story hardens the a11y layer on top and confirms the responsive degrade.

architecture.decision: No design fork. Layout (CSS grid two-pane + @media 820px collapse) already lives in theme.css; a11y focus ring already exists. This story is additive: (1) CSS-only hardening of target sizes, reduced-motion, and contrast across the existing stylesheets; (2) a global keyboard-play handler in App that routes through the EXISTING handlePad(padId) and onTogglePlay so pad capture/sound and transport all stay on one code path. No new component, no state model change.
seams: Keyboard play routes through the existing App.handlePad(padId) (so REC capture + sound stay identical to a tap) and App.onTogglePlay (transport). A single window keydown effect maps 12 physical keys to PAD_IDS in order and Space to play/stop. It must ignore auto-repeat, modifier combos, and typing targets.

Reduced-motion: the moving cues (beat-dot.is-current, step-cell.is-playhead) get a subtle CSS pulse as the motion cue for 'hit-now'; a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block removes the animation and leaves the static outline/glow so the cue still reads by shape, not motion or hue.

Target size + contrast are token/stylesheet tweaks in theme.css / TransportControls.css / StepGrid.css. Primary controls (.tbtn transport/mode/bank/octave) reach >=44px. The 32-cell grid is a deliberately dense editor: cells meet the 24px AA minimum where the pane allows and are noted as the density exception; they stay keyboard-operable buttons.

tasks.title: a11y CSS baseline: >=44px targets, reduced-motion cue, contrast check, confirm responsive collapse
tasks.intent: Harden the existing stylesheets (src/theme.css, src/TransportControls.css, src/BeatIndicator.css, src/StepGrid.css) for the a11y baseline WITHOUT changing the layout structure or component markup: (1) TARGET SIZE — give every .tbtn (transport, mode, bank, octave −/+ buttons) a min-height and min-width of 44px (keep current padding/appearance; center content); ensure the octave readout stays visually aligned. (2) GRID DENSITY — the 32-step .step-cell is a dense editor: give cells a min-height so they meet the 24px AA target minimum vertically while the row width stays fluid; add a `/* ponytail: dense sequencer grid — cells meet the 24px AA target min vertically; 44px per cell is impossible at 32-across, an accepted density exception */` comment. (3) REDUCED MOTION — add a subtle CSS pulse animation (a gentle box-shadow/opacity pulse, ~1s ease-in-out infinite) to `.beat-dot.is-current` and `.step-cell.is-playhead` as the 'hit-now' MOTION cue, then add a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that sets `animation: none` on those and keeps the existing static outline/glow so the cue still reads by shape. (4) CONTRAST — verify --text and --text-dim meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text) against their backgrounds (--bg, --surface); if --text-dim (#9a9a94) falls below 4.5:1 on any real usage, nudge it lighter just enough to pass and note it. Do NOT alter the accent hue. (5) Confirm the two-pane grid still collapses at <=820px to a single stacked pane (leave the existing @media as-is unless it is broken).
tasks.constraints: CSS-ONLY — do not touch .tsx files or component structure. Keep the stealth theme + Anthropic-orange single accent; brightness/glow encodes state. The reduced-motion cue must degrade to a NON-animated but still-visible cue (outline/shape), never disappear. Cues carry shape + motion, never color alone (playhead already has an outline; keep it). Reuse existing CSS variables/tokens; add no new color unless a contrast bump requires nudging --text-dim. Keep diffs minimal and commented where non-obvious.
tasks.acceptance: npm run build passes. In the browser: at desktop width both panes render side by side; at <=820px they stack to a single pane without overflow/breakage. Every .tbtn computes to >=44px in both dimensions. A pulse animation is present on the current beat dot and playhead, and is removed under prefers-reduced-motion (media rule present, static cue remains). --text/--text-dim pass AA against their backgrounds. No console errors.

StepGrid.css: .step-cell min-height 24px (density-exception ponytail comment), @keyframes ph-pulse on .is-playhead + reduced-motion block animation:none (static outline kept). tasks.title: Keyboard play — map physical keys to pads + Space toggles transport
tasks.intent: Add desktop keyboard play in src/App.tsx via a single window keydown effect: map 12 physical keys to PAD_IDS in order — use the top letter row `q w e r t y u i o p [ ]` (index 0..11 → PAD_IDS[0..11]) — and call the EXISTING handlePad(padId) for a match so sound + REC capture behave exactly like a tap. Map Space to onTogglePlay (play/stop). Also add a small, unobtrusive on-screen hint line (e.g. under the existing status line) describing the keys, so the feature is discoverable and screen-reader legible. Register the listener in a useEffect with proper cleanup; use a ref or the existing callbacks so the handler always sees current mode/octave/recording (handlePad already closes over current state on each render — if you attach/detach the listener each render it stays fresh, or keep handlers in refs; pick the simplest correct approach and note it).
tasks.constraints: IGNORE the event when: e.repeat is true (no machine-gun auto-repeat), any modifier is held (ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey), or the event target is a typing element (input/textarea/[contenteditable]) — none exist today but guard anyway. For Space: preventDefault to stop page scroll, but do NOT hijack Space when a button/interactive control is focused (so Space still activates a focused button) — e.g. only toggle transport on Space when document.activeElement is the body or a non-interactive element. Route pad keys through handlePad (do not duplicate audio/capture logic). Keys are case-insensitive. Keep the diff minimal, TypeScript strict, and do not regress stories 1.1–1.5 (pad clicks, grid, transport, octave, REC). Mark the key map with a ponytail comment; the authentic per-key layout tuning can come later.
tasks.acceptance: npm run build passes. In the browser: pressing q/w/e/... triggers the matching pad (the 'Pad: X' readout updates and audio fires, same as a click); with PLAY running + REC armed a key press captures to the grid at the current step just like a tap; pressing Space toggles the transport (PLAY⇄STOP) when no control is focused and does not scroll the page; auto-repeat (holding a key) does not retrigger continuously. No console errors. The on-screen key hint is visible.
tasks.visual: Browser: focus the page body, dispatch/press a mapped pad key (e.g. 'q') → the 'Pad:' readout shows pad 1 and no console error; press Space → transport toggles to STOP (probe playing state or the button label), press Space again → back to PLAY; confirm holding a key (e.repeat) does not spam. Screenshot showing the key-hint line and a played pad state.
